title: Post-Expiry Notice Make-Good on Domain Registrations Restores
content:
# Service standard: the post-expiry notice make-good

Harborline sends the registrant of a Domain Registrations domain a post-expiry notice after the expiry date. On a redemption restore billed on or after 1 December 2025, the notice record on the domain decides a make-good on the amount of that restore.

**Clause.** The notice make-good is USD 3.00 where no post-expiry notice dated on or after the expiry date recorded on the domain is on file, USD 1.50 where the latest post-expiry notice is dated more than the TLD's post-expiry notice period (the number of calendar days after the expiry date within which that notice is sent: 5 calendar days for each of .us, .ca, .com, .org, .net, .co and .io Domain Registration) after that expiry date, and nothing where it was sent within that time.

| Post-expiry notice record on the domain | Make-good |
|---|---|
| No post-expiry notice dated on or after the recorded expiry date | USD 3.00 |
| Latest post-expiry notice dated more than the TLD's notice period after the expiry date | USD 1.50 |
| Latest post-expiry notice dated within the TLD's notice period | Nothing |

### Reading the record
- The date compared is the expiry date recorded on the domain. A post-expiry notice dated before that date (for instance from an earlier expiry) does not count as a notice on file for this purpose.
- Where several post-expiry notices are on file, the latest one decides between the second and third rows.
- The boundary is inclusive on the "within" side: a notice dated exactly on the last day of the notice period is within that time; a notice dated one day later is late.

*Hypothetical case (dates chosen for illustration):* a .net domain with an expiry date of 11 October 2028, where the notice period is 5 calendar days. A latest post-expiry notice dated 16 October 2028 (day 5) earns nothing; one dated 17 October 2028 (day 6) earns USD 1.50; no post-expiry notice dated on or after 11 October 2028 earns USD 3.00.
